utterances.text: "Kept one copy for myself 1992," and then I placed a note there, "unlawful" meaning unlawful order. Perhaps I should have added the word order or content. However, there was not enough space for that to be written there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Some of the entries, very quickly, I'm spending rather too much time on this, say copies from records. For example number 44, what is that from? What records? Not from the archive.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might be that this is a document that was in the records of either in the protocol department or somewhere else, but anyway, I would need to see the document itself in order to be able to give you a more precise answer. If you can give me a minute, maybe I can trace it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: As I say I'm spending rather too long on this. Finally, on this question of documents, you provided us -- all of us with an extra, I think, rough estimate was 180-odd separate documents. I'm just trying to find my note for them. But anyhow, where did those new documents come from? Were they all at home?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes those documents were with me and if you wish we can clarify them one by one. So the information bulletin was made out in the necessary number of copies and one can often see that one copy was addressed to the chief, Andrija. So literally one copy, apart from the register and apart from all other chiefs of department, was dedicated for the chief of the centre, and, therefore, I kept it. Secondly, if you follow security information and intelligence concerning paramilitary units and their activities, also one copy was prepared for the chief and very often it was written by hand to be sent to the chief of CSB or to Chief Andrija or they didn't even write anything, but I was entitled to have a copy each and that is how I kept them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, I am sorry, but again there are two questions. Why did you keep all these documents or selected out of the huge amount of correspondence that went through the CSB?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already explained about some of those documents, i.e., the documents that were unlawful or had unlawful contents. Some of them I kept to be used, as I said earlier, for cross-referencing information with military security service. That's why I had them with me. And let me tell you this, I never gave up on the intention that one day I write something about everything that was happening at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And the last question on these is: Are you actually allowed to keep copies of all these documents at your home as a serving member of the MUP between 1991 and now?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: There's nothing that stops every single member of the MUP taking home and keeping in his home, without any kind of security precautions, internal MUP documents, is that what you are telling the Court?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the way you put it, but one could keep a copy; and when I say one, I meant myself. I didn't take any documents from the official records, but I just kept certain copies for myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want to now move from documents in the short time we have left today to deal with the beginnings of your employment with the MUP. You told the Court that you were seven years with the secretariat for national defence in Derventa; that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you were then asked by Mr. Zecevic, forgive me, I'm just going to get hold of the transcripts. And this is at page 19417. It was put to you that you started working at the Ministry of the Interior of the socialist republic when, and you said I believe it was in early May or perhaps the end of April, and looking at your notebook May would be -- seems to be right. You were asked: "Did you apply for the job? Was there a vacancy announced and how did you get the job?" And you actually didn't answer the first part of the question because you went straight into the procedures about the selection of the three candidates, and so on and so forth. Now, you were asked the same question when you were interviewed, I think, in 2004. The trouble with grey binders is that they all look the same. And this is at page 16 of the first interview which is T-002550. You were asked by Mr. Sabir: "Were you contacted first by this political party, that's SDS, before they nominated you as a candidate?" And you said: "Yes. And the way it was done, there were some who were favourites and there were some who were outsiders." Then you explained it was Mr. Ninkovic, rather than you. And you were asked: "Do you remember when you were contacted by the SDS in order to discuss your candidacy for the position as head of CSB Doboj?" And you said: "I think I was contacted in March or April, and that also was one of the reasons that made me join at least these people, these candidates. At that time deputy minister of the interior, Dr. Zepinic, was a man I knew from before." It's to do with sports: "Q. You discussed your candidacy to the CSB Doboj with Mr. Zepinic? "A. Yes." Is that all correct, Mr. Bjelosevic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you then went on to say this, although the officer after the tapes were changed said: "Q. You were describing," and this is at page 17, "that you were contacted in March 1991 by the SDS. Do you remember by whom you were contacted from the SDS? "A. By the late Milovan Bjelosevic, who was my cousin. He was deputy at the National Assembly at that time." So Mr. Bjelosevic, just so we can get this right, who contacted you first, Mr. Bjelosevic and then you discussed it with Mr. Zepinic, or was it the other way around?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall exactly what the order was, but, yes, I talked to both of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Whether or not you were actually a member, a paid up member of the SDS, were you sympathetic to the aims of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partly, yes, and I can tell you exactly what it was. In the manifesto, the Serbian Democratic Party made it clear that they would advocate the preservation of Yugoslavia. I believe that to be a crucial part of their programme, and I believe that everyone who was in favour of preserving Yugoslavia was close to my heart. And ultimately I was trained to serve my country and my country was Yugoslavia. And I did everything I could to preserve this country. Yes, I was sympathetic with this particular part of their orientation and programme.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, you said that you were not the candidate that they wanted. They wanted Mr. Ninkovic who was head of the SDS in Doboj. And you pointed to the letter that was written by the SDS, which I suppose we better have up again. It's ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tab 1A.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, I made a note.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, this is dated the 29th of May, 1991, so it's after you've been appointed, and it's addressed to the Municipal Assembly, Executive Boards, Sarajevo MUP, and the chiefs of the public security station and the SDS Main Board. And if we go over the page, we see the decision.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it says attach --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry. We haven't gone over the page on the screen, please. Could we go to the next page, please, on the screen in each, B/C/S and English.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: There are signatures appearing. First of all, from Derventa, your cousin; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, only his signature was forged, the late Milovan did not sign this. I can bring you a paper where you can see his signature, how it actually looks like. But they believe that it would be important to have as many signatures as possible. He was not at this meeting and the late Milovan specifically told me that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, did he do anything about it? If his signature was forged, did he write a letter saying my signature has been forged?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if he wrote any letter. He only told me that he wasn't at that meeting, and I know his signature so this is not his signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I mean, you've answered one of the questions I was going to ask you, which is: Why should the man who suggested you take the job sign saying you were the wrong person? The only other question I want to ask you about this is Tesic, the man who signs is Dusan Kuzmanovic. Is that the same Dusan Kuzmanovic who was head of the SJB in Teslic in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So, to your knowledge, at least one of the chiefs of the SJBs was a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Kuzmanovic was a member of the SDS. I even believe that for a time he was the president of the Municipal Board or a member of the Municipal Board. But apart from that, I know that he was a member, without doubt.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And it's a fact, isn't it, Mr. Bjelosevic, that although technically no member of the MUP should have been a member of a political party once the communists were, as it were, disbanded, not disbanded, that's not the right word, a number of police officers did join the SDS and no doubt the SDA and the SDZ?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably. However, I don't recall that there was any ban in that sense at the time, i.e., that anyone was banned from being a member of any political party in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I mean, Mr. Bjelosevic, I'm perfectly prepared to accept that my understanding was that police officers were not supposed to be joining political parties in 1990 and 1991, but if you say there was no ban, I'm perfectly prepared to accept that. Now, I want to deal --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Maybe I don't, because, Your Honours, I'm going to move to something that requires documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, we are about to take the adjournment for today but we aren't going to rise immediately, so the usher would escort you from the courtroom and we would resume your cross-examination tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just ask what shall I do with these documents?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, in fact, I was going to ask whether Mr. Bjelosevic would be prepared to leave his notebooks with us. What I think we are going to try to do, subject to any difficulties that we are told about, is scan them in colour. At the moment, we've got rather poor copies sometimes in black and white, so Mr. Bjelosevic is prepared to hand them over to us and we'll just scan them, if we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, is that a problem?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't mind. Only I want them back after you are finished.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, they will certainly be returned to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may just one minute -- brought something to your attention. Your Honours, you will remember that Mr. Hannis asked for one week to file his complaint on the footnotes of expert witness Bajagic. Now, we discussed over the weekend -- over yesterday, actually, and today, a number of the footnotes that -- or the list of the footnotes that we intend to offer, and we deleted a number of these footnotes and we are still, so to speak, talking, the Defence and the Office of the Prosecutor. However, Your Honours gave the dead-line today, and I would kindly ask, actually, on behalf of Mr. Hannis, but it is joint effort by Defence and the Office of the Prosecutor, that dead-line be extended until tomorrow afternoon. Thank you very much. JUDGE HALL. Tomorrow afternoon would be sufficient?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: No, I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, I'm sure we will be able to deal with that in the afternoon today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we so extend it. Thank you. On the 10th of May, the Trial Chamber accepted Stevo Pasalic as an expert in demography for the Defence. Stevo Pasalic subsequently testified on the 10th to the 13th of May and the Stanisic Defence has requested admission into evidence of his expert report. On the 13th of May, the Prosecution objected, arguing that the report only addresses Serb population movements and that his testimony has not explained their relevance to the displacement of non-Serbs. It submitted that Stevo Pasalic is "less well acquainted with war influenced migrations of non-Serbs" and that he does not have sufficient knowledge of non-Serb populated areas, and that the report is "essentially a tu quoque report." In response the Stanisic Defence submitted that Stevo Pasalic's report should be considered complementary to that of the Prosecution expert and that the Chamber by having access to both reports would, and I quote, "have a broader basis to rely on." On the 13th of May, the Prosecution also requested that the Chamber reconsider its ruling that Stevo Pasalic be considered an expert in demography, submitting that its cross-examination had raised such serious doubts about his expertise that reconsideration would be warranted. The Chamber, recalling the 10th of May ruling was issued in the exercise of its discretion, holds that the Prosecution has not demonstrated a clear error of reasoning or that it would be necessary to reconsider the ruling to prevent an injustice. Accordingly, it reaffirms the 10th of May ruling that Stevo Pasalic is considered to be an expert in demography. Stevo Pasalic's report appears to be confined to analysing the displacement of Serbs, while the present trial is concerned with the alleged deportation and forcible transfer of non-Serbs. Moreover, the methods employed cast doubt on the integrity of some of his conclusions. The Chamber notes the submissions of the Stanisic Defence that Stevo Pasalic's evidence and report are to be considered complementary to the evidence of the Prosecution's demographer. While the Chamber does not necessarily accept this submission, it holds that the report would be of assistance in its analysis of the body of evidence before it. And it will be a matter for the Chamber at the appropriate time to be determined the weight to be given to the report in light of the trial record as a whole. The report is accordingly admitted into evidence. So we take the adjournment -- yes, so it should be assigned an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this will be Exhibit 1D541.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. And we take the adjournment until tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 18th day of May, 2011 at 9.00 a.m.
